title: Dante's journey
hook: midway through life's journey, lost in a dark wood, Dante is led by love through hell, purgatory and heaven
carry: the love that moves the sun

segments.voice: Yesterday, the Beguines, living side by side behind a city gate, and your line was women together.

In the middle of the journey of our life, I found myself in a dark wood, for the straight way was lost. That's how a long Christian poem begins, put into plain English. A man halfway through his life wakes up lost, with no idea how he got there. The wood is wild and thick. He sees a hill with sunlight on it and tries to climb, and wild animals drive him back down. He is stuck. Then someone appears to help. The man is the poet Dante, writing about himself.

The poem is known as the Divine Comedy. The help that comes in the wood is the ghost of Virgil, an old Roman poet, sent because Beatrice, a woman Dante loved who has died, asked for him. So the journey starts with love reaching down into the dark. Virgil leads Dante down through hell, where people are stuck forever in the shape of their choices. Then up a mountain, purgatory, where souls are being healed and made ready, climbing slowly, even singing. Then Beatrice herself guides him up through the heavens. The way out of the dark wood isn't straight up the sunny hill. It goes down first, and only then up. The poem is honest about pain. In heaven, Dante's ancestor tells him what's coming: he'll be driven out of his city, Florence. He'll learn how salty another man's bread tastes, and how hard it is to climb another man's stairs. Then the last line. Dante sees God, and can't describe it. All he can say is that his desire and will were turned, like a wheel, by "l'amor che move il sole e l'altre stelle." The love that moves the sun and the other stars. The poem began in a dark wood. It ends at the center of everything, with love. Christians read it in different ways: as a story, a map of the soul, a vision.

Ask quietly where you are on your own journey, in a dark wood, going down through something hard, climbing slowly, or somewhere bright, and name it in a word or two, with nothing to fix. Then ask who has been your Virgil, someone who helped you find the way. If you pray, bring that place and that person to God; if not, hold them both for a moment.
Dante's journey. A poet lost in a dark wood, led by love down through hell, up the mountain of purgatory, and into heaven.
Your line: the love that moves the sun. The dark wood was only the beginning. On to tomorrow.

howItsDone: Christians and other readers take up Dante's Divine Comedy as poetry and as a spiritual journey, and some churches and reading groups go through it slowly, a canto at a time.

chat.says: I heard the Divine Comedy is all about hell. Is that right?
options: Hell's only the start. It goes down, then up through purgatory, and ends with the love that moves the sun.
Mostly. Dante wrote it to frighten readers, and the poem ends at the very bottom of hell.
No, it's a funny story about the afterlife; that's why the title calls it a comedy.
chat.meaning: Dante's poem goes from a dark wood down through hell, up the mountain of purgatory, into heaven, and ends with the love that moves the sun.
